Tim Cook's tenure as Apple CEO is entering its final weeks, with John Ternus set to officially take over the company's top role on September 1. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan believes Ternus could usher in a bolder, more risk-taking era for Apple.

John Ternus is expected to take bigger risks on new products, acquisitions, and R&D after becoming CEO

Apple's CEO transition is nearly complete. So far, the company has heavily emphasized the continuity Ternus will bring to the role.

However, not everyone on Wall Street is convinced Ternus will follow Cook's playbook quite as closely.

In a research report obtained by this publication, Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated a strong "Buy" rating on Apple. A key part of that rating hinges on the expectation that Ternus will continue Cook's legacy while having a greater "risk tolerance." Mo Farooq writes:

The bank highlighted that Apple's decision to abandon its net cash neutral goal is an early signal that management may be more willing to deploy capital. This would translate into higher R&D spending, more capital expenditures, and potentially larger acquisitions — all areas that were not mainstays of Cook-era strategy. Bank of America believes that under Ternus, Apple could move more aggressively into new product categories, including AI glasses, AirPods with cameras, smart rings, smart home devices, personal assistants, and robots.

Ultimately, Bank of America believes Ternus will continue Cook's legacy of building Apple into a global, highly profitable machine, but expects he will leverage the company's strong position of strength to make bolder moves going forward.

Once Ternus takes over as CEO, we may not see any major changes immediately. But perhaps in the coming months, any potential differences in priorities will start to become clearer.

What are your expectations for John Ternus as Apple's CEO? Let us know in the comments.
